Pricing
Context is free. Two things you can pay us to run.
The apps are free and your notes live in storage you own. What costs money is infrastructure we operate for you — and only if you want it.
Free, always
·
Every app, every AI client, every note.
·
Storage you own — an S3 bucket or your Dropbox.
·
Taking everything with you, whenever you want.
Premium
$20 a month, for one brain or one workspace
Pick either of these, or both. The price is the same either way, and it covers the one brain or workspace you choose it for — not your account, and not every context you can reach.
Managed storage
A bucket we create and pay for, up to 50 GB. Yours to take away at any time.
Fast search
An index of this context's notes, kept in a database we run, so search answers in milliseconds. Your Markdown never moves.
A workspace has one payer and any number of members: whoever owns it pays once, and everybody in it gets what it is paying for.
You can turn Premium on later, on whichever context needs it.
Taking your notes with you is free, on both plans, and keeps working after you cancel. Cancelling makes a context read-only and exportable — it never deletes anything.

Context.LC — build decisions

Context.LC — build decisions

Tenancy is bucket-level, never prefix-level. No key
namespacing inside a customer bucket, so an existing
brain connects with zero migration and Obsidian
Remotely Save keeps working.

A shared context is just a workspace with more than
one member — so a storage binding hangs off a
workspaceId, never a userId.

Saved in your bucket

Free first, then the two things $20 buys. The billable unit is on the price itself.

  • ships todayPrice, ceiling and entitlement copy come from the shipping module
  • proposed hereA pricing surface anywhere in the product
  • ships todaySign-up from here

Three options, free ones first, price on the face of the paid one. The variant this pack recommends.

  • ships todayThe two free cards, and skipping
  • proposed hereThe managed card and everything behind it
  • proposed hereThe line under the card still reads "your notes stay in a bucket you own" — true on two of three paths and false on the third. The chrome's own copy has to change with this screen; the replacement is in the copy deck.

Ask the question the cards answer, then show one branch. The alternative, kept for the critique.

  • proposed hereThe whole screen

The last screen before Stripe: what it costs, what it covers, what it is not, and where you are going.

  • ships todayEntitlement rows, hint and price
  • needs backend workSelecting entitlements before a plan row exists
  • proposed hereThe confirmation step itself

The URL arrives a beat after the press, so the departure is its own moment — with a way out if it never arrives.

  • ships todayTwo round trips, and the press that leaves
  • proposed hereThe slow-mint case having any UI at all

Stripe's cancel URL lands somewhere that says nothing was charged, and offers the free paths.

  • ships today`cancel_url` is set
  • needs backend workA route that answers it (today it is `/settings`, which is not a route)
  • proposed hereThis screen

The webhook has not landed. Never says failed, never spins without a sentence, and gives permission to leave.

  • ships todayThe webhook that ends this wait
  • needs backend workA return route, and a way to watch a plan turn active
  • proposed hereThis screen

A minute later. The work finishes server-side whether or not this tab is open, and the copy says so.

  • ships todayServer-side completion independent of the tab
  • proposed hereA support path that can finish it by hand

The managed bucket being created and scaffolded. Named steps rather than a bar, because there is no honest percentage.

  • ships todayBucket naming and the guards around the managed account
  • needs backend workThe provisioning action itself
  • proposed hereThis screen

Paid, and no storage. Says the money and the notes are safe, says retry cannot duplicate, and offers the free path out.

  • ships todayRetry being idempotent (the bucket is named from the workspace id)
  • needs backend workA retry control, and a subscription that can be stopped from here
  • proposed hereThis screen

Ends in the next onboarding step rather than in a tick, and restates the hand-off in the same breath.

  • ships todayThe layout step this hands to
  • needs backend workThe hand-off it points at

The real panel against a free fixture. Nothing here is a drawing.

  • ships todayEverything on this frame

Both entitlements, a renewal date, a note census, and the manage-billing press that leaves for Stripe.

  • ships todayEverything on this frame
  • needs backend workAnything actually consuming the entitlement

The owner is told their card was declined and where to fix it. Nothing is deleted, and the panel says so.

  • ships todayEverything on this frame
  • needs backend workThe context going read-only as a result

The same state, seen by somebody who does not hold the card: no decline, no date, no buttons.

  • ships todayEverything on this frame

The upgrade path for a context that already has notes somewhere. The hazard is silent data loss, so the copy is about what is copied and what is left alone.

  • ships todayReading the current binding and its provider
  • needs backend workCopying an existing context's notes into managed storage
  • proposed hereThis screen

The promise, as two controls. Marked: neither is built, and non-negotiable #1 makes both launch blockers for managed storage. It is drawn under Premium here because that is the seam this prototype renders through — it belongs under Storage, or on its own row, where a free context can reach it too.

  • ships todayThe promise, in words, in every state
  • needs backend workA download of everything
  • needs backend workHanding a managed bucket to storage the customer owns

Past due on a managed context. The way out is on the banner, not three screens away.

  • ships todayThe plan status behind it
  • needs backend workA write path that actually goes read-only
  • proposed hereThe banner

Same state, no card detail, no controls — the narrowing `describePremium` already performs, carried out of settings.

  • ships todayThe narrowing rule
  • proposed hereThe banner

Not an alarm. States what is true — readable, exportable, never deleted — and offers both ways forward.

Frames marked ships today are the running product rendered against a fixture, not a drawing of it. Nothing in this document can reach an account, a bucket or a card: it has no backend behind it at all.
